intent: Change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, with the five-sensor row unchanged at y=0.08 and x spread ±0.06, to test whether a larger footprint keeps more tape in view at the edge and stops the once-per-run slalom line loss. wheel_track stays at 0.10 m, which the iteration 5 result supports. Expected: slalom line_loss_events below 1.0 and slalom progress above 0.10, the s-bend holding the iteration 5 gains (progress at least 0.42), and the oval finish rate at or above 0.85.
learning: Iteration 5 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 raised s-bend progress from 0.17 to 0.42 and cut s-bend line losses, while the oval stayed at a 1.0 finish rate. The s-bend still drifts to about 0.062 m, and the slalom still loses the line once per run. These point to two separate limits: turn rate on the s-bend, and sensor coverage on the slalom. Ask the Integrator: on the slalom, do the outer sensors read near zero at the line loss, and at which direction change does it happen? On the s-bend, is max_error reached on the first or second bend? If the larger footprint raises oscillation on the oval, the next step is to return sensor_size to 0.012 and look at sensor y or x spacing instead.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 m, everything else held at iteration 3 values) moved the s-bend from progress 0.17 to 0.42 and cut its line losses to 0.1 per run. The s-bend still leaves the track at max_error 0.0624, just above the 0.06 m limit, so the turn-rate change helped but did not finish the bend. The oval is fine at 20 of 20 finishes, progress 0.998 and max_error 0.037, so I keep wheel_track at 0.10 and do not return to 0.11. The slalom still loses the line once per run (line_loss_events 1.0) and leaves the track at progress 0.0975. This matches the Integrator's decision rule: the s-bend is drift at about 0.061 m, and the slalom is still losing the line once per run, so the next step is slalom sensor coverage. I change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, keeping the same five-sensor row at y=0.08 with x spread ±0.06, so the footprint covers more tape at the edges where the line is lost. The 0.016 footprint at x=±0.06 still sits inside the body envelope (about ±0.068 m reach, against the ±0.06 body half-width plus margin). Body, wheels and mass stay the same, since the off-track floor binds at 0.06 m for all body widths. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events falls below 1.0 and slalom progress rises above 0.10, with the oval finish rate holding at or above 0.85. A risk is that the larger footprint blurs the line-edge signal, which could raise oscillation on the oval, so I ask for oscillation to be measured.
